concepts.def: Poetics: tragic hero's error or flaw causes downfall; Othello's jealousy, Macbeth's ambition, Lear's pride.
Purgation of pity and fear in audience; tragedy's moral function; debated by AC Bradley (1904).
Moor of Venice manipulated by Iago into killing Desdemona; race, jealousy, manipulation; tragic Othello restores honour.
Aged king divides kingdom by daughters' flattery; Cordelia banished, Goneril and Regan turn; tragic recognition of madness.
Shakespearean Tragedy; character-based criticism; tragic hero exceptional but flawed; lasting influence.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Critics differ on the central flaw. F. R. Leavis saw Othello's self-dramatising egotism as the engine; A. C. Bradley emphasised his noble nature deceived.

Modern critics often add race, class and military culture to the answer.

The temptation scene is the play's peripeteia. Iago's hints, the handkerchief and Othello's escalating jealousy drive the reversal.

The scene's length and density of staged emotion make it one of the great Shakespearean set pieces.
Act V delivers anagnorisis (Othello realises Iago lied), catastrophe (the murder of Desdemona, Othello's suicide), and ritual closure (Lodovico's verdict on Iago).
